title: Jared Spool audited a major retailer and found one thing killing conv...
description: Jared Spool audited a major retailer and found one thing killing conversions. Not pricing. Not shipping. A register button. 160,000 password reset requests a day. Customers leaving because they couldn't remember which account they'd used. They swapped it for one word. Continue. Sales went up 45% in month one. The problem was never the customer. It was a door nobody thought to remove. What friction are you still asking people to push through? #Ecommerce #UXDesign #ConversionOptimization #DigitalMarketing
transcript: A major e commerce retailer had car abandonment problem. They brought in a UX researcher named Jared Spool to find out why what he found stopped everyone in the room. 45% of their customers had multiple accounts on the same site and they can remember which one they'd use. Password reset requests were hitting hundred and sixty thousand per day. One register button. That was the entire problem. It sat between the customer and the purchase. And millions of people just left. They removed the register button, replaced it with one word continue. Added one line. You don't need a create account to make purchases on our website. Sales went up 45%. 15 million extra in month one, 300 million in year one. Was the register button legally required? No. Required by a payment processor? No. It was inherited UX from a different era. And it cost him 300 million before someone finally asked why was it there? So how much is your version of that button worth?
